1. The accused is facing trial for offences u/s 279/337/338 IPC.

The genesis of the prosecution story is that on 18.10.2011, at about 3:15 PM at Ring Road, near WHO building, Delhi within the jurisdiction of PS IP Estate, accused was found driving car bearing no. DL-3CBF-7409 in rash manner and endangering the life and safety of others and caused grievous injuries to Vijay Singh Malik and Suman Kumar and caused simple injuries to Sheetal and Anil Gupta.
Thereafter, the alleged offending vehicle was taken into possession by the police after which its mechanical inspection was conducted.
It is stated in the chargesheet that the alleged offending vehicle was being driven by accused at the relevant time.
After completion of investigation, the chargesheet for offences u/s 279/337/338 IPC was submitted for trial of accused.

4.
In order to establish guilt of the accused, prosecution has examined 13 witnesses in all.

driver of said tempo namely Sheetal and he sustained injuries.

Estate.
On that day, he joined the investigation in this case.

He alongwith the IO reached at the spot State vs Naresh Gupta on 9 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/98269053/

On that day, he received DD no. 18 A regarding the accident at Ring Road WHO Building ITO, Delhi.
He alongwith Ct. Ibrahim reached at spot, where Tempo no. DL 1LM 4622 and car no. DL 3CBF 7409 were found in accidental condition.
He was taken into custody and handed over to Ct. Ibrahim.
The PCR already had taken the injured person to hospital.
He left Ct. Ibrahim at spot with accused for supervision of spot and he went to hospital where he collected the MLC of injured persons Vijay Kumar Malik, Suman, Sheetal Sada and others.
He recorded the statement of injured Sheetal Sada.
Thereafter, he returned at spot alongwith complainant.
He prepared rukka and got registered the case through Ct. Ibrahim who went to P.S. and got registered the FIR.
He inspected the site at the instance of the complainant and prepared site plan.
Ct. Ibrahim again came at the spot, who gave him copy of FIR and rukka.
The accused was arrested at the identification of complainant.
He seized offending car and truck TATA 407.
He seized the document of car and said truck.
He also seized the D/L of accused.
Both the vehicles were taken to PS.
Both the vehicles were mechanically inspected and he collected the mechanical inspection reports.
He recorded the statement of witnesses.
The MLC of injured person were deposited for obtaining the nature of injury.
The nature of injury on the MLC of injured Suman was opined grievous, therefore, he added section 338 IPC.
Thereafter the investigation was transferred to MACT Cell, Central, Delhi and he returned the case file to MHC(R).
This witness was cross-examined by Ld. counsel for defence.
4.10 PW-10 Inspector Suman Kumar deposed that it was 18.10.2011.
He was posted as SI at the office of Food and Supply Dept. GNCT Delhi.

Dr. Vivek Kumar deposed that on 09.12.2011, he was posted at Sir Ganga Ram Hospital in Plastic and Cosmetic Surgery(Unit-2) as a Consultant.
On that day, he advised the patient namely Vijay Singh Malik for follow up vide letter no. MRD/1/2011 dated 09.12.2011.

Dr. Arvind deposed that on 18.10.2011, he was posted at LNJP Hospital as CMO in accident and emergency department.

Dr. Yogesh deposed that he was a summoned witness to depose on behalf of Dr.

5. Thereafter, PE was closed and matter was fixed for recording of statement of accused.

6. After prosecution evidence, the statement of accused u/s 281 Cr.PC r/w 313 Cr.P.C was recorded wherein all the incriminating circumstances were put to him to which he stated that he is innocent and he had been falsely implicated in the case.

Accused opted not to lead DE.
7.
Thereafter, matter was fixed for final arguments.
8. Ld. counsel for the accused argued that accused was not driving the vehicle negligently and the accident was caused due to negligence of complainant and injured persons.
He further argued that site plan was not prepared at the instance of complainant and no public witness has been cited as witness.
He further argued that there are contradictions in the testimony of PW-1 and PW-4.
With these submissions, he prayed that benefit of doubt be given to the accused.
Per contra, Ld. APP for the State argued that there is sufficient material available on record to render conviction to the accused as the guilt of the accused has been proved beyond reasonable doubt.

9. ANALYSIS AND FINDINGS:
1 Allegations against the accused are for offence under Section 279/337/338 IPC.
2 Section 279 IPC provides that "Whoever drives any vehicle, or rides, on any public way in a manner so rash or negligent as to endanger human life, or to be likely to cause hurt or injury to any other person, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to six months, or with fine which may extend to one thousand rupees, or with both".

5 3

In order to prove the case against the accused, the prosecution was under the obligation to prove the following essential ingredients of the offence punishable u/s 279/337/338 IPC:
 a Identity of the accused being the  driver of the offending vehicle.
 b
That the alleged accident is the result of rash and negligent driving of the accused at a public place.
c The rash and negligent driving of the accused resulted in the injuries incurred by the injured persons namely V.S. Malik, Anil Gupta, Shyambir Singh and Suman Kumar.

RE: IDENTITY OF THE ACCUSED:
10.
It is not in dispute that accused was driving offending bearing no. DL-3CBF-7409 at the time of the alleged incident nor the presence of accused has been disputed by the defence.
PW-9 SI Joginder deposed that accused was found present on the spot when he reached at the spot and his car was found in accidental condition and he was taken into custody from the spot itself.

Further, vide statement dated 05.01.2024, accused admitted that he was the registered owner of the offending vehicle and he further undertook that he would not raise any objection qua the identity of the vehicle.
Further, PW-1 V.S. Malik also deposed that the driver of the offending vehicle was apprehended from the spot.
The mechanical inspection report of the offending vehicle is Ex. PW3/A which reflects fresh damages.
Therefore, the presence of accused alongwith his vehicle in the accidental condition proves that accused was driving the offending vehicle at the time of the accident.
RE: ALLEGED ACCIDENT IS THE RESULT OF RASH AND NEGLIGENT DRIVING OF THE ACCUSED AT A PUBLIC PLACE.

11. Now coming to the defence that the accident was not caused by the negligence of accused, it is observed that PW-1 Vijay Singh Malik, PW-2 Shyambir Singh, PW-4 Anil Gupta and PW-10 Suman Kumar are the injured eye witnesses who gave coherent testimonies.
PW-1 V.S. Malik deposed that he alongwith Inspector Suman Kumar and Inspector Shyambir went to the spot to check the truck bearing no. DL-1LM-4622 at the instance of informer Anil Gupta.

PW-4 Anil Gupta deposed that he informed Sh. V.S. Malik about the presence of a truck carrying wheat and accordingly, PW-1 Sh. V.S.
Malik alongwith his team members came at the spot.
Their presence on the spot is confirmed by way of medical evidence which are the MLCs Ex. P1 to P5.
All of them were taken to LNJP Hospital by PCR Van as deposed by PW-6 ASI Satpal and PW-5 Retired SI Sukhbir Singh.

The minor contradictions in the testimony of PW-1 and PW-2 on the aspect i.e. who was standing behind the truck and who was trying to the climb the truck is immaterial when their presence near the truck is proved.

6 12.

sentences.text: Further, Ex. PW9/C is the site plan prepared by the IO.

Point A is the accidental spot where the accident took place and the point A reflects that the truck bearing no. DL-1LM-4622 was stationed at the left most side of the road and it was not stationed in between the road raising any inference that the accident was due to the contributory negligence of injured persons.

The record further reflects that PW-9 IO SI Joginder Singh deposed that the site plan was prepared at the instance of complainant but complainant Sheetal Sada could not be examined as he got expired during the trial.

The non availability of complainant for deposition does not vitiate the case of prosecution or the site plan prepared by the IO when IO clearly deposed that the site plan was prepared at the instance of complainant.

13. Further, Ex. PW3/A is the mechanical inspection report of the offending vehicle and it reflects that the vehicle was damaged from the front right side and it further reflects that the vehicle was entirely damaged from the front.
Further, PW3/B is the mechanical inspection of the truck bearing no. DL-1LM-4622, near which the injured persons were standing at the time of accident.
The mechanical inspection report reflects that the truck was damaged from the rear left side.

Both the mechanical inspections reports indicate that indeed a collision took place between the offending vehicle bearing no. DL-3CAF-7409 and truck bearing no. DL-1LM-4622 and it was the offending vehicle which dashed into the truck from behind leaving no scope of any other possibility that accident might have caused due to the fault of truck driver.
The truck was not in the moving condition and it was stationed as deposed by all the public witnesses and mechanical inspection reports have been duly proved by PW-3 Manohar Lal.
14. Further, Ex. P4 is the MLC of Anil Gupta as per which he incurred simple injury.
Ex. PW11/A is the medical certificate issued in respect of PW1 Vijay Singh Malik as per which he sustained grievous injuries.
Similarly, Ex. A3(Colly) are the medical documents of PW-2 Shyambir indicating that PW-2 Shyambir sustained a fracture.
The MLCs have been duly proved by PW-12 Dr. Arvind who was posted as CMO at the time of incident.

15. The testimony of PW-1 V.S. Malik, PW-2 Shyambir Singh, PW-4 Anil Gupta and PW-10 Inspector Suman Kumar are unimpeachable as there are only minor contradictions and they being injured eye witnesses, their testimony has to stand on a higher pedestal.
Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in case titled as Shyam Babu Vs. State of UP, AIR 2012 SC 3311, held that the testimony of injured witness stands on higher pedestal.

entities.text: Shyam Babu Vs. State of UP, AIR 2012 SC 3311
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Furthermore, there is no reason to disbelieve the version of all the injured witnesses or their presence at the place of occurrence as they were directly taken to the hospital and their MLC was conducted.

The medical evidence alongwith ocular testimony of all eye witnesses namely PW-1, PW-2, PW-4 and PW-10 show that they were present near the vehicle,
on the spot.
16. In nutshell, from the testimonies of the aforesaid witnesses examined by the prosecution, the alleged occurrence of accident due to rash or negligent act of the accused stands proved.

In view of the foregoing discussion, this Court is of the considered view that the prosecution has proved the case beyond all reasonable doubts that on the given date, time and place, the accused was driving the vehicle no. DL-3CBF-7409 and that too, in a rash or negligent manner so as to endanger human life or public safety of others, therefore, accused is convicted for the offence u/s 279 IPC.
